21:1: Adonoy said to Moshe; speak, to the kohanim, the sons of Aharon, and you shall say to them, let him not defile himself with the dead among his people.

AND the Lord spake to Mosheh, saying: Speak unto the priests, the men of the children of Aharon, that they keep themselves apart from defilement and thus shalt thou say to them: For a man who is dead, (the priest) shall not defile himself among his people;
21:2: Except to his kin to whom he is closely related, for his mother and his father, for his son, his daughter and for his brother.
but for a woman who is of kin to his flesh, for his daughter, and for his father, and for his son, and for his daughter, and for his brother,
21:3: For his virgin sister, to whom he is closely related, who has not yet been married, for her, he may be defiled.
and for his sister, a virgin who is nigh to him, and who hath neither been betrothed, nor married to a husband, for her he may defile himself.
21:4: A husband [An honored one among his people] may not defile himself among his people [for a wife through whom] he becomes profaned.
The husband shall not defile himself on account of his wife, except so far as it is right for him; but for a relative of those who do the work of his people he may defile himself.
21:5: They shall not make baldness on their heads and the corners of their beards they shall not shave, and they shall not make gashes in their flesh.
They shall not mark themselves between their eyes, nor set a mark upon their heads, nor cut away the corners of their beards, nor make any incision in their flesh:
21:6: They shall be holy to [before] their God and they shall not profane the Name of their God, for [it is] the fire-offerings [offerings] of Adonoy, the bread [sacrifice] of their God [that] they bring [offer], and they must [therefore] be holy.
but they shall be holy before their God, and shall not profane the name of their God;
21:7: A harlot [One who strays] or a profaned woman they shall not marry. A woman divorced from her husband they shall not marry, for he is holy to [before] his God.

They shall not take to wife a woman who hath gone astray by fornication, or who was born illegitimate, nor a woman who hath been put away, whether from her husband or the husband's brother, may they take; for he is to be holy before his God.
21:8: You shall make him holy for he offers the bread [sacrifice] of your God; he shall be holy unto you for I, Adonoy, am holy, Who makes you holy.
Thou shalt sanctify him unto the priesthood; for the oblation itself of thy God he is to offer: he shall be holy to thee, and thou shalt not make him profane: I, the Lord who sanctify you, am holy.
21:9: The daughter of a kohein, who profanes herself by fornication [straying]—she profanes her father—[she becomes profane with respect to her father’s holiness] she shall be burned with fire.

And if the betrothed daughter of a man of the priesthood profane herself, by going astray in fornication; if, while she is yet in her father's house, she is guilty of fornication, she shall be burned with fire.
21:10: The kohein who is greatest among his brethren upon whose head was poured the anointing oil [which inaugurates to greatness]; whose hands [sacrifices] were consecrated [offered] to put on the special garments; shall not let his hair grow wild and he shall not tear his garments.

And the high priest who hath been anointed over his brethren, and upon whose head the anointing oil was poured, and who offered his oblation to be arrayed in the (holy) robes, shall not make his head bare, nor either rend or tear his garment in the hour of grief.
21:11: And adjacent to any dead body he shall not enter. For his father and mother he shall not become [ritually] impure.
Nor unto any person who is dead shall he go in, nor for his father or his mother make himself unclean.
21:12: He shall not depart from the Sanctuary and he shall not profane his Gods Sanctuary, for the crown of his Gods anointing oil [which inaugurates to greatness] is upon him, I am Adonoy.
And he shall not go forth from the sanctuary, or profane the sanctuary of his God; for the anointing oil of his God is upon him: I am the Lord.
21:13: And he shall take a wife who is in her virginity;
21:14: A widow, divorcee, profaned woman or harlot [one who strays]; he may not marry [any] of these. But only a virgin from his own people may he marry.

but a widow, or a divorced person, or one who was born of depraved parents, or who hath gone astray by fornication, such as these be shall not take; but a virgin proper shall he take to wife from the daughters of his people.
21:15: He shall not profane his offspring among his people, for I am Adonoy, who makes him holy.
Neither shall he profane his offspring among his people; for I the Lord do sanctify him.
21:16: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
21:17: Speak to Aharon saying; Anyone of your offspring, through [all] their generations who will have a blemish, shall not approach to offer the bread [sacrifice] of [before] his God.
Speak with Aharon, saying: No man of thy sons in the families of their generations who hath a blemish in him shall be qualified to offer the oblation of his God:
21:18: For any man who has a blemish shall not approach; a blind man or a lame man, or a man with a sunken nose, or a man who has disproportionate limbs.
for no man who hath a blemish in him shall offer. A man who is blind or lame, or stricken in his nostrils, or mutilated in his thigh,
21:19: or a man who has a broken (crippled) foot, or a broken (crippled) hand,
or a man who hath a broken foot, or a broken hand
21:20: or one with overhanging eyebrows, or with a cataract, or a disarrangement [in the eye], or one with scurf or scabs, or one with crushed testicles.

or whose eyelids droop so as to cover his eyes, who hath no hair on his eyelids; or who hath a suffusion of whiteness with darkness in his eyes; or who hath the dry scurvy, or who is full of the blotches of Egypt, or whose testicles are swollen or shrunk,
21:21: Any man who has a blemish, who is a descendant of Aharon the kohein, shall not approach to offer the fire-offerings [offerings] of Adonoy. He has a blemish; the bread [sacrifice] of his God he may not approach to offer [as an offering].

no man, a priest of the race of Aharon the priest who hath in him any such blemish, shall be qualified to offer the oblations of the Lord. He hath a blemish, and it is not meet for him to offer the oblation of his God.
21:22: The bread of his God which is of the most holy, and from the holy [offerings] he may eat.
Nevertheless he may support himself with the residue of the oblations of his God which remaineth of the most holy and of the holy (offerings);
21:23: However, he may not enter beyond the Curtain and he shall not approach the Altar for he has a blemish and he shall not profane My holy things, for I am Adonoy, who sanctifies them.
only he must not enter within the veil, nor approach the altar; for a blemish is in him, and he shall not profane My sanctuary; for I the Lord do sanctify them.
21:24: Moshe spoke [these words] to Aharon, and to his sons and to all of Bnei Yisroel.
And Mosheh spake with Aharon and with his sons, and with all the sons of Israel.
22:1: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
22:2: Speak to Aharon and to his sons and let them keep away from the holy offerings of Bnei Yisroel and they shall not profane My holy name which they sanctify for [before] Me, I am Adonoy.

Speak with Aharon and with his sons, that they keep apart from the consecrated things of the children of Israel, and profane not the Name of My Holiness (in whatever) they hallow before Me: I am the Lord.
22:3: Say to them; throughout your generations; any person of your offspring who will draw near to the holy things which Bnei Yisroel will sanctify to [before] Adonoy [while] his impurity is on him that soul [person] shall be cut off from My Presence, I am Adonoy.

Say to them, Take heed in your generations: whatever man of all your sons who shall offer things hallowed, which the children of Israel have consecrated before the Lord, having his uncleanness upon him, that man shall be destroyed with a stroke of death before Me: I am the Lord.
22:4: Any man of Aharons offspring; who has tzoraas [the plague of ’confinement’] or an impure flow, may not eat of the sacred things until he has purified himself. [The same is true] of anyone who touches anything defiled by the dead [soul], or anyone who has had a seminal emission,

Any man, young or old of the offspring of Aharon, who is a leper, or hath a running issue, shall not eat of things consecrated till he be clean: and whoever toucheth any uncleanness of man, or one from whom uncleanness hath proceeded,
22:5: or anyone who touches any creeping creature that causes impurity to him, or any person which causes impurity to him, [with] whatever impurity he has.
or who toucheth any reptile that maketh unclean, or (the corpse of) a dead man which maketh unclean, or any of the uncleanness of his life,
22:6: Anyone touching [that person] will be impure until the evening. He shall not eat of the holy things unless he has washed his body in water.
the man being a priest who toucheth such shall be unclean until the evening, and may not eat of the holy things, except that he wash his flesh in forty seahs of water.
22:7: When the sun sets, he is pure, and afterwards, he may eat of the holy things, for it is his bread.
And when the sun hath set and he be fit, he may afterward eat of the holy things; for they are his food.
22:8: An animal which has died on its own, or an animal that was fatally maimed, he must not eat to defile himself with it, I am Adonoy.
But of a dead carcase, or (that which hath been) killed (by violence), he may not eat to defile himself therewith. I am the Lord.
22:9: They shall keep my charge [the charge of My Word] lest they bear [the burden] of sin and die because of it for having profaned [it]. I am Adonoy Who makes them holy.

But the sons of Israel shall observe the keeping of My Word, that they may not bring sin upon themselves, nor die for it by the flaming fire; because they have profaned it: I am the Lord who sanctify them.
22:10: No stranger (non-kohein) may eat holy things. One indentured to a kohein and one hired [by a kohein] may not eat sacred-offerings.
No stranger or profane person shall eat of a consecrated thing, (neither) a son of Israel who is an inmate of the priest, nor any hireling, may eat of the hallowed thing.
22:11: If a kohein shall purchase a person [as a slave, that person is] his monetary possession. He may eat of it, and the [slave] born in his house, they may eat of his bread.
But if the priest buy a man a stranger with the price of his money, he may eat of it, and such as have grown up in his house may eat of his bread.
22:12: When a koheins daughter marries a non-kohein, the sacred terumah [separated] portions may not be eaten by her.
And the daughter of a priest, if she be married to a man a stranger, may not eat of things set apart by consecration.
22:13: If a koheins daughter is either widowed or divorced, and she has no children, and she returns to her fathers home as in her youth, she may eat of her fathers bread. No non-kohein may eat of it.

But if the daughter of a priest be a widow, or be divorced and having no child by him hath returned to her father's house, and hath not been wedded to a brother-in-law, (Deut. xxv. 5,) she, being as in the days of her youth, and not being with child, may eat of her father's meat; but no stranger shall eat thereof.
22:14: If a man inadvertently eats of sacred-offering, he shall add a fifth, to it[s worth] and give to the kohein the holy thing.
And if a man of Israel eat that which is consecrated unknowingly, let him add a fifth part of its value to it, and give the (price of the) holy thing unto the priest.
22:15: They shall not profane the holy things of Bnei Yisroel that which they designated for [before] Adonoy.
Let them not profane the sacred things of the children of Israel which are set apart unto the Name of the Lord,
22:16: They burden them[selves] with the sin of their guilt when they eat their holy things [in impurity], for I am Adonoy, Who makes them holy.
nor let the sin of their trespass be found upon them, by eating in uncleanness their consecrated things; for I am the Lord who do sanctify them.
22:17: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
22:18: Speak to Aharon and to his sons and to all of Bnei Yisroel and say to them; any man of the House of Israel, and from the proselytes of Israel who will bring his offering for any of their vows or for any of their free-will-offerings that they will bring to [before] Adonoy, for a burnt-offering.

Speak with Aharon and with his sons and with all the children of Israel: -A man, whether young or old, of the house of the family of Israel, or of the strangers who are in Israel, who shall offer his oblation of any of their vows, or their free will offerings which they present before the Lord for a burnt sacrifice,
22:19: To gain acceptance [it must be] an unblemished male of cattle, sheep or goats.
to be acceptable for you, it shall be perfect, a male of the bullocks, of the lamb, or of the young goats.
22:20: Anything that has a blemish on it you shall not bring, for it will not be accepted favorably for you.
But anything that hath a blemish you shall not offer; for that will not be acceptable from you.
22:21: If a man will bring a peace[sacred]-offering to [before] Adonoy, to fulfill an articulated vow or free-will-offering of cattle or of sheep, it shall be unblemished, that it be favorably accepted. No blemish shall be in it.

And if a man will offer a consecrated victim before the Lord to fulfil a vow, or as a free will offering, from the herd, or from the flock, it must be perfect to be acceptable; no blemish shall be in it.
22:22: A blind, broken-limbed, cracked or wart[ed animal]; or [an animal] with scurf or scabs you shall not bring these to [before] Adonoy; and as a fire-offering [an offering] you shall not place of them on the altar of [before] Adonoy.

Whatever is blind, or broken-boned, or stricken in the eyelids, or whose eyes are stricken with a mixture of white and dark, or one filled with scurvy or the blotches murrain, you shall not offer before the Lord, nor present an oblation of them on the altar before the Lord.
22:23: An ox or lamb with one limb larger [or smaller] than the other or with uncleft hooves [one limb smaller than the other], you shall make (offer) it as a free-will-offering [to the temple treasury] [but] for [the fulfillment of] a vow it will not be favorably accepted.
A bullock or a ram that hath superfluity or deficiency of the testicles, you may make a free will offering, but for a vow it will not be acceptable.
22:24: [An animal that has its testicles] crushed, mangled, torn or cut off you shall not bring to [before] Adonoy and in your land you shall not inflict these injuries.
That which is crushed, or ruptured, or diseased, or enervated, you shall not offer to the Name of the Lord; and in your land you shall not emasculate.
22:25: And from a strangers [gentiles] hand you shall not bring (offer) the bread [offering] of your God from any of these for they have inflicted wounds in them; they will not be favorably accepted for you.

And from the hand of a son of the Gentiles you shall not offer the oblation of your God of any of these, because their corruption is in them; a blemish is in them, they are profane, they shall not be acceptable for you.
22:26: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying
22:27: An ox, lamb or goat, when it is born, shall be with its mother for seven days. From the eighth day and thereafter it may be favorably accepted as a sacrifice as a fire-offering to [an offering before] Adonoy.

(to the effect that): What time thou callest to our mind the order of our oblations, as they shall be offered year by year, being our expiatory offering for our sins, when on account of our sins (such sacrifices are required), and we have none to bring from our flocks of sheep, then shall a bullock be chosen before him, in memorial of the righteousness of the elder who came from the cast, the sincere one who brought the calf, fat and tender, to Thy Name. A sheep is to be chosen, secondly, in memory of the righteousness of him who was bound as a lamb on the altar, and who stretched forth his neck for Thy Name's sake, while the heavens stooped down and condescended, and Izhak beheld their foundations, and his eyes were blinded by the high things; on which account he was reckoned to be worthy that a lamb should be provided for him as a burnt offering. A kid of the goats is to be chosen likewise, in memorial of the righteousness of that perfect one who made the savoury meat of the kid, and brought it to his father, and was made worthy to receive the order of the blessing: wherefore Mosheh the prophet explaineth, saying: Sons of Israel, my people, When a bullock, or a lamb, or a kid is brought forth according, to the manner of the world, it shall be seven days after its dam, that there may be evidence that it is not imperfect; and on the eighth day and thenceforth, it is acceptable to be offered an oblation to the Name of the Lord.
22:28: An ox [cow] or a [female] lamb, it and its [her and her] offspring, you shall not slaughter in one day.
Sons of Israel, my people, as our Father in heaven is merciful, so shall you be merciful on earth: neither cow, nor ewe, shall you sacrifice along with her young on the same day.
22:29: When you sacrifice a thanks-giving-offering to [before] Adonoy, that it be favorably accepted for you you shall sacrifice it.
And when you offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving to the Name of the Lord, you shall offer so as to be accepted.
22:30: On that day [that it is sacrificed] you should eat it; you shall leave none of it until the next morning, I am Adonoy.
It shall be eaten on that day, none shall remain till the morning: I am the Lord.
22:31: You shall preserve My commandments and fulfill them, I am Adonoy.
And you shall observe My commandments to do them I am the Lord who give a good reward, to them who keep My commandments and My laws.
22:32: You shall not profane My holy Name; but I will be sanctified among Bnei Yisroel. I am Adonoy Who makes you holy.
Nor shall you profane My Holy Name, that I may be hallowed among the children of Israel. I am the Lord who sanctify you,
22:33: Who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God, I am Adonoy.
having brought you forth redeemed from the land of Mizraim, that I may be to you Eloah: I am the Lord.
23:1: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
23:2: Speak to Bnei Yisroel and say to them; the appointed times of Adonoy, which you shall proclaim [cause] them [to occur] as holy assemblies [occurrences]; these are My appointed times.
Speak with the sons of Israel, and say to them, The orders of the time of the Festivals of the Lord, which you shall proclaim as holy convocations, these are the orders of the time of My festivals.
23:3: Six days shall work be performed; and on the seventh day is a Shabbos of resting, a holy assembly [occurrence]. You shall not do any work, it is a Shabbos for [before] Adonoy in all your dwelling places.
Six days shalt thou do work, and the seventh day (shall be) a Sabbath and a rest, a holy convocation. No manner of work may you do; it is a Sabbath to the Lord in every place of your habitations.
23:4: These are the appointed times of Adonoy, the holy assemblies [occurrences] that you shall proclaim [cause] them [to occur] in their appointed times.
These are the times of the Festivals of the Lord, holy convocations which you shall proclaim in their times:
23:5: In the first month (Nisan), on the fourteenth day of the month in the afternoon, is a Pesach (offering) for [before] Adonoy.
In the month of Nisan, on the fourteenth day of the month, between the suns (shall be) the time for the sacrifice of the Pascha to the Name of the Lord.
23:6: On the fifteenth day of this month is the festival of matzos, for [before] Adonoy; for seven days you shall eat matzos [matzoh].
And on the fifteenth day of this month the feast of unleavened cakes to the Name of the Lord. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
23:7: On the first day [there] shall be a day of holy assembly [occurrence] for you; you shall not do any work of labor.
On the first day of the feast a holy convocation shall be to you; ye shall do no work of labour,
23:8: You shall bring a fire-offering to [an offering before] Adonoy [on each of] seven days. On the seventh day it is [a day] of holy assembly [occurrence]; you shall not do any work of labor.
but offer the oblation to the Name of the Lord seven days; in the seventh day of the feast shall be a holy convocation; you shall do no work of labour.
23:9: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
23:10: Speak to Bnei Yisroel and say to them; when you come into the land that I give to you and you reap its harvest, you shall bring an omer of the first fruits of your harvest to the kohein.

Speak with the sons of Israel, and say to them: When you have entered into the land which I give you, and you reap the harvest, you shall bring the sheaf of the first fruits of your harvest unto the priest;
23:11: He shall wave [lift up] the omer before Adonoy that it be favorably accepted for you. On the day after the day of rest (Pesach), the kohein shall wave [lift] it [up].
and he shall uplift the sheaf before the Lord to be accepted for you. After the first festal day of Pascha (or, the day after the feast-day of Pascha)
23:12: You shall prepare, on the day when you wave [lift] the omer, an unblemished, male, yearling lamb as a burnt-offering, to [before] Adonoy.
on the day on which you elevate the sheaf, you shall make (the sacrifice of a lamb of the year, unblemished a burnt offering unto the Name of the Lord:
23:13: Its meal-offering is two tenths of flour mixed with [olive] oil as a fire-offering to [an offering before] Adonoy of pleasing fragrance [to be accepted with favor]. Its wine-offering is one fourth of a hin.
and its mincha, two tenths of flour, mingled with olive oil, for an oblation to the Name of the Lord, to be received with acceptance; and its libation, wine of grapes, the fourth of a hin.
23:14: Bread, parched grain or tender [ground] grain you shall not eat until this very day, until you bring the offering of your God; it is an everlasting statute for all your generations in all your dwelling places.

But neither bread nor parched corn (of the ripe harvest) nor new ears may you eat until this day, until the time of your bringing the oblation of your God: an everlasting statute unto your generations in all your dwellings.
23:15: You shall count for yourselves, from the day after the day of rest (Pesach) from the day on which you will bring the omer waveuplifted-offering, seven complete weeks they shall be,
And number to you after the first feast day of Pascha, from the day when you brought the sheaf for the elevation, seven weeks; complete they shall be.
23:16: Until the day after the seventh week, you shall count fifty days, and you shall bring a new meal-offering to [before] Adonoy.
Until the day after the seventh week you shall number fifty days, and shall offer a mincha of the new bread unto the Name of the Lord.
23:17: From [the land of] your dwelling places you shall bring two bread wave[uplifted]-offerings; of two tenths of flour they shall be. You shall bake them leavened, as first-fruit-offering to [before] Adonoy.
From the place of your dwellings you are to bring the bread for the elevation; two cakes of two-tenths of flour, which must be baked with leaven, as first fruits unto the Name of the Lord.
23:18: You shall bring, along with the bread, seven unblemished, yearling lambs, one young bullock and two rams; they shall be a burnt-offering to [before] Adonoy with their meal-offerings and wine-offerings, a fire-offering of pleasing fragrance to [an offering which is accepted with favor before] Adonoy.

And with that bread you are to offer seven lambs of the year, unblemished, and a young bullock without mixture (of colour), the one for a sin offering, and two lambs of the year for a sanctified oblation.
23:19: You shall prepare one he-goat as a sin-offering and two yearling lambs as peace[sacred]-offerings.
And you shall make (a sacrifice) of a young goat without mixture, the one for a sin offering and two lambs of the year for a sanctified oblation.
23:20: The kohein shall wave [lift] them [up] along with the bread of the first-fruit-offering as a wave-offering [an uplifted-offering] before Adonoy with the two lambs; they shall be holy for [before] Adonoy, for the kohein.
And the priest shall uplift them with the bread of the first fruits, an elevation before the Lord, with the two lambs; they shall be holy to the Name of the Lord, and shall be for the priest.
23:21: You shall proclaim [cause to occur] on this very day; it shall be a [day of] holy assembly [occurrence] for you you shall not do any work of labor. It is an everlasting statute in all your dwelling places throughout your generations.

And you shall proclaim with life and strength that self-same day, that at the time of that day there shall be to you a holy convocation: you shall do no work of labour: it is an everlasting statute in all your dwelling for your generations.
23:22: When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not cut completely the corner of your field when you reap. You shall not gather the gleaning of your harvest. You shall leave them for the poor and the proselyte, I am Adonoy, your God.

And when you reap the harvest of the ground, you shall not finish one corner that is in thy field at thy reaping nor shalt thou gather the gleanings of thy harvest, but leave them for the poor and the strangers: I am the Lord thy God.
23:23: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
23:24: Speak to Bnei Yisroel, saying; in the seventh month, on the first of the month, shall be for you a [day of] rest. A remembrance of the sounding [crying] [of the shofor], a holy assembly [occurrence].
Speak with the children of Israel, saying: In Tishri, which is the seven month, shall be to you a festival of seven days, a memorial of trumpets, a holy convocation.
23:25: You shall not do any work of labor and you shall bring a fire-offering to [an offering before] Adonoy.
No work of labour may you do, but offer an oblation before the Lord unto the Name of the Lord.
23:26: And the Lord spake with Mosheh saying:
23:27: Indeed, on the tenth day of this seventh month is a day of atonement. It shall be for you a [day of] holy assembly [occurrence] and you shall afflict yourselves and you shall bring a fire-offering to [an offering before] Adonoy.

But on the tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement; a holy convocation shall it be to you, and you shall humble your souls, (abstaining) from food, and from drink, and from the use of the bath, and from anointing, and the use of the bed, and from sandals; and you shall offer an oblation before the Lord,
23:28: You shall not do any work on this very day, for it is a day of atonements, to atone for you before Adonoy, your God.
and do no work on this same day; for it is the Day of Atonement, to make atonement for you before the Lord your God.
23:29: For any person who will not be afflicted on this very day shall be cut off from his people.
For every man who eateth in the fast, and will not fast that same day, shall be cut off by death from among his people.
23:30: Any person who does any work on this very day, I will cause that person to perish from among his people.
And every man who doeth any work on that same day, that man will I destroy with death from among his people.
23:31: You shall not do any work; it is an everlasting statute for all your generations in all your dwelling places.
No work of labour may you do an everlasting statute for your generations, in all your dwellings.
23:32: It is a Shabbos of complete rest for you and you shall afflict yourselves on the ninth day of the month at evening; from evening to evening you shall rest, on your day of rest.

It is a Sabbath and time of leisure for you to humble your souls. And you shall begin to fast at the ninth day of the month at even time; from that evening, until the next evening, shall you fast your fast, and repose in your quietude, that you may employ the time of your festivals with joy.
23:33: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
23:34: Speak to Bnei Yisroel saying; on the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the festival of [shelters] Sukkos for seven days, for [before] Adonoy.
Speak with the sons of Israel: In the fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the Feast of Tabernacles, seven days unto the Name of the Lord.
23:35: On the first day [there shall be] a holy assembly [occurrence]; you shall not do any work of labor.
On the first day of the feast is a holy convocation; no work of labour may you do.
23:36: For seven days, you shall bring a fire-offering to [an offering before] Adonoy; the eighth day shall be for you a holy assembly [occurrence], and you shall bring a fire-offering to [an offering before] Adonoy. It is [a day] of convocation. you shall not do any work of labor.
Seven days you shall offer an oblation to the Name of the Lord, you shall gather together to pray before the Lord for rain; no work of labour may you do.
23:37: These are the appointed times of Adonoy which you shall proclaim [cause] them [to occur] [as] holy assemblies [occurrences], on which to bring a fire-offering to [an offering before] Adonoy; a burnt-offering and a meal-offering, a [sacred-]sacrifice and wine-offerings, each on its assigned day,

These are the times of the order of the Lord's festivals which you are to convoke for holy convocations, to offer an oblation to the name of the Lord, a burnt sacrifice and a mincha, sanctified offerings and libations, the rite of a day in its day;
23:38: Besides the [offerings of the] Shabbasos of Adonoy and besides your gifts and besides all your vow-offerings and besides all your free-will-offerings that you will give to [before] Adonoy.
beside the days of the Lord's Sabbaths, beside your gifts, and beside your vows, and beside your free-will offering which you bring before the Lord.
23:39: Indeed, on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you gather the produce of the land you shall celebrate the festival of [before] Adonoy for seven days. The first day is a day of rest and the eighth day is a day of rest.

But on the fifteenth of the seventh month, at the time when you collect the produce of the ground, you shall solemnize a festival of the Lord seven days. On the first day, rest; and on the eighth day, rest.
23:40: You shall take for yourselves, on the first day, the fruit of the beautiful tree (esrog) [esrogim], a branch of palm trees (lulav) [lulavim], boughs of thick-leaved trees (hadasim), and willows of the brook (aravos), and you shall rejoice before Adonoy, your God, for seven days.

And of your own shall you take on the first day of the feast, the fruits of praiseworthy trees, citrons, and lulabin, and myrtles, and willows that grow by the brooks; and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God seven days.
23:41: You shall celebrate it as a festival to [before] Adonoy seven days in the year; it is an everlasting statute throughout your generations in the seventh month, you shall celebrate it.
And you shall solemnize it before the Lord seven days in the year, by an everlasting statute in your generations shall you observe it in the seventh month.
23:42: You shall dwell in the [shelters] sukkos seven days, every native born [settled] Israelite shall dwell in the [shelters] sukkos.

In tabernacles of two sides according to their rule, and the third a handbreadth (higher), that its shaded part may be greater than that into which cometh the sunshine; to be made for a bower (or shade) for the feast, from different kinds (of materials) which spring from the earth and are uprooted: in measure seven palms, but the height within ten palms. In it you shall sit seven days; the males in Israel, and children who need not their mothers, shall sit in the tabernacles, blessing their Creator whenever they enter thereinto.
23:43: So that your generations will know that in the [clouds of shelter] sukkos I caused Bnei Yisroel to dwell when I took them out from the land of Egypt, I am Adonoy, your God.
That your generations may know how, under the shadow of the cloud of glory, I made the sons of Israel to dwell at the time that I brought them out redeemed from the land of Mizraim.
23:44: And thus Moshe declared the [order of the] appointed times of Adonoy [and taught them] to Bnei Yisroel.
And Mosheh declared the time of the orders of the Lord's festivals, and taught them to the sons of Israel.
24:1: And the Lord spake with Mosheh,saying:
24:2: Command Bnei Yisroel to take (bring) to you pure, pressed, olive oil for illumination to keep the lamp [lamps] burning constantly.
Command the children of Israel that they bring of their own, pure beaten olive oil for the light, that the lamps may burn continually, on the day of Sabbath, and on the day of work;
24:3: Outside of the Curtain of the Testimony, which is inside the Tent of Meeting, Aharon shall arrange it [so that it burns] from evening until morning before Adonoy, continually; as an everlasting statute throughout your generations.

outside of the veil of the testimony for evermore, because the Shekinah dwelleth in Israel: in the tabernacle of ordinance shall Aharon order it from evening till morning before the Lord continually, by an everlasting statute unto your generations.
24:4: Atop the pure menorah he shall arrange the lights before Adonoy, constantly.
24:5: You shall take fine flour and bake twelve loaves, each individual loaf shall be two tenths [of an ephah].
And thou shalt take flour, and bake thereof twelve cakes, according to the twelve tribes; two tenths shall be one cake.
24:6: You shall place them in two stacks, six in each stack on the Pure Table, before Adonoy.
And thou shalt set them in two orders (rows), six in one order, and six in the other upon the table in its purity, as it is ordained before the Lord.
24:7: You shall put pure frankincense on [each] stack and it shall be as a memorial portion for the bread, as a fire-offering, to [an offering before] Adonoy.
And thou shalt put upon the orders pure frankincense, that it may be an oblation of memorial bread before the Lord.
24:8: On each and every Shabbos he shall arrange them before Adonoy, continually, from [before] Bnei Yisroel as an eternal covenant.
From Sabbath day to Sabbath day he shall order it anew before the Lord continually from the children of Israel. This shall be an everlasting statute.
24:9: It shall belong to Aharon and to his sons and they shall eat it in a sacred place, for it is most holy for him from among the fire-offerings [offerings] of Adonoy, as an everlasting statute.

And it shall be for Aharon and for his sons, and they shall eat it after they have taken it from off the table in the holy place; for it is most sacred to him of the oblations of the Lord by an everlasting statute.
24:10: The son of an Israelite woman went out, and he was the son of an Egyptian man, among Bnei Yisroel. They argued in the encampment—the son of the Israelite woman, and the Israelite man.

But a wicked man, a rebel against the God of heaven, had come out of Mizraim, the son of the Mizraite man who had killed the man of Israel in Mizraim, and had gone in unto his wife, who conceived and bare a son among the children of Israel. And while the Israelites were dwelling in the wilderness, he had sought to spread his tent in the midst of the tribe of the children of Dan; but they would not permit him, because in the arrangements of Israel every man dwelt with his family by the ensigns of the house of their fathers. And they contended together in the camp, and the son of the Israelitess with a man of Israel, who was of the tribe of Dan, went to the house of judgment;
24:11: The Israelite womans son clearly pronounced the Name [of God] and blasphemed [caused anger] and they brought him to Moshe. The name of his mother was Shlomis, daughter of Divri of the tribe of Dan.

and when they had come out from the house of judgment, where he had been condemned, the son of the daughter of Israel expressed and reviled the great and glorious Name of Manifestation which he had heard at Sinai, and defiled and execrated; and the name of his mother was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibree, of the tribe of Dan.
24:12: They placed [bound] him in the guardhouse until [his penalty] would be explained to them through the [law of the] word of Adonoy.

This is one of four judgments which were brought in before Mosheh the prophet, who decided them by the dictate of the Word, who is above. They were judgments about money and about life. In judgments on money Mosheh was prompt; but in the judgment on life he was deliberate (or slow by delay) each (party) Mosheh said, I have not heard: that he might teach the chiefs of the Sanhedrin of Israel, who were to arise after him, to be prompt in judgments respecting money, but slow in judgments that affected life; and not to be ashamed to inquire for counsel in cases that should be too hard for them, forasmuch as Mosheh, Rabban of Israel, had need to say, I have not heard. Therefore they shut him up in the house of confinement till the time that it should be explained to them by the decree of the Word of the Lord.
24:13: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
24:14: Take the blasphemer [one who has caused anger] beyond the encampment, and all those who heard him shall lay their hands on his head and the entire congregation shall stone him.
Bring forth the blasphemer without the camp, and let the witnesses who heard his blasphemy, and the judges, lay their hands upon his head, and let the whole congregation stone him with stones.
24:15: And to Bnei Yisroel you shall speak, saying; Any person who shall blaspheme [cause anger before] his God shall bear [the burden of] his sin.
And speak thou with the sons of Israel, saying: A man young or old who shall blaspheme the known Name of his God shall bear his sin.
24:16: Whoever pronounces clearly the Name of Adonoy [and blasphemes] he will surely be put to death. The entire congregation shall surely stone him. The proselyte and native born [settled one] alike when he clearly articulates the Name, shall be put to death.

Whosoever expresseth and revileth the Name of the Lord shall verily be put to death; all the congregation shall cast stones upon him, whether he be a sojourner or native-born, when he hath blasphemed the Name that is Alone, he shall die.
24:17: Any man who kills any human being must surely be put to death.
And if a man destroy the life of any one of the children of Israel, he shall verily be put to death by the sword.
24:18: Whoever kills an animal shall pay for it, [the compensation of] an animal for an animal.
And he who destroyeth the life of an animal shall make it good, a living animal for a living one.
24:19: A man who maims his neighbor just as he did, so shall be done to him.
And a man who inflicteth a blemish on his neighbour, whatsoever he hath done it shall be done unto him:
24:20: [Compensation for] a broken bone [in exchange] for a broken bone, [compen-sation for] the loss of an eye [in exchange] for the loss of an eye, [compensation for] the loss to a tooth [in exchange] for the loss of a tooth; just as he maimed the man, so shall it be done to him [monetarily].
the value of a fracture for a fracture; the value of an eye for an eye; the value of a tooth for a tooth; whatsoever blemish he inflicteth upon the man, the same shall be rendered unto him.
24:21: Whoever smites [kills] an animal shall pay for it. Whoever smites [kills] a person shall be put to death.
He who killeth a beast shall restore it; but be who slayeth a man shall be slain.
24:22: One rule shall apply for all of you just as it is for the proselyte, so it shall be for the native born [settled one], for I am Adonoy, your God.
One judgment shall you have for the stranger and for the native; for I am the Lord your God.
24:23: Moshe spoke to Bnei Yisroel and they took the blasphemer [one who caused anger], beyond the encampment and they stoned him with a stone. And Bnei Yisroel did just as Adonoy commanded Moshe.

And Mosheh spake with the sons of Israel, and they brought forth the blasphemer without the camp, and stoned him with stones; and the sons of Israel did it, by laying their hands upon, leading him away hanging, and burying him, as the Lord had commanded Mosheh.
25:1: Adonoy spoke to Moshe on Mount Sinai, saying;
AND the Lord spake with Mosheh in the mountain of Sinai, saying:
25:2: Speak to Bnei Yisroel and say to them, when you come to the land which I give to you the land shall be at rest—a Shabbos for [rest before] Adonoy.
Speak with the children of Israel, and say to them: When you have entered into the land that I will give to you, then shall the ground rest for a rest before the Lord.
25:3: For six years you shall plant your field and for six years you shall prune your vineyard and you shall harvest its produce.
Six years you shall sow your fields, and six years prune your vineyards and gather in the fruit;
25:4: But the seventh year shall be a Shabbos of [complete] rest for the land, a Shabbos for [rest before] Adonoy, you shall not plant your field and you shall not prune your vineyard.
but in the seventh year there shall be a rest of remission to the earth, that she may rest before the Lord; you shall not sow your fields, nor prune your vineyards.
25:5: [Even] crops that grew on their own [from the seeds of your previous] harvest you shall not reap, and the grapes of your untended vines you shall not gather; it shall be a year of complete rest for the land.
The after crop which remaineth from your harvests you may not reap, nor of your later grapes make a vintage; a year of remission it shall be unto the earth;
25:6: The [produce] [rest] of the lands Shabbos[-year] [land] shall be for yourselves, for food, for you, your servant and your maidservant, for your hired hand and your resident sojourner who reside with you.
but the remission of the ground shall be to you for food, to thee, to thy servant, and to thine handmaid, and to thy hireling, and to the stranger who dwelleth with thee;
25:7: [Also] for your domesticated animals and for the [wild] beasts that are in your land shall all of its produce be for food.
and for thy cattle and for the animals that are in thy land shall be the produce of it (also).
25:8: You shall count for yourself seven sabbatical years [of rest], seven years, seven times and it shall be for you, the days (period) of the seven sabbatical years [of rest], forty-nine years.

And thou shalt number to thee seven Sabbaths of years, seven times seven years, and they shall be to thee the sum of the days of seven Sabbaths (or remissions, shemittin) of years, forty and nine years.
25:9: You shall make a proclamation [crying] with the shofor on the tenth day of the seventh month. On Yom Kippur shall this shofor-proclamation be made. throughout all your land.

And thou shalt make the voice of the trumpet to sound a jubilee in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, on the Day of the Expiations thou shalt make the voice of the trumpet of Liberty to pass through all your land.
25:10: You shall sanctify the year of the fiftieth year and proclaim freedom in the land for all of its inhabitants; it shall be for you a jubilee and each man shall return to his ancestral land and each man shall return to his family.

And you shall sanctify that year, the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty in the land of Israel to all the inhabitants; Jubela shall it be to you, and you shall return every man to his inheritance, and every man unto his family, you shall return.
25:11: It is a jubilee, [that] the year of the fiftieth year shall be for you. You shall not plant and you shall not reap [even] crops that grew on their own; and you shall not gather the [grapes of] its untended vineyard,
The year of Jubela shall that fiftieth be to you: ye shall not sow, nor reap the after crop, nor make vintages of the grapes which have been let alone.
25:12: For it is a jubilee, it shall be holy to you. Whatever is in the field, you may eat of its produce.
For that Jubela shall be sacred to you, the produce of the field shall you eat.
25:13: On this jubilee year, each man shall return to his ancestral land.
In this year of Jubela you shall return every man unto his inheritance.
25:14: If you sell anything to your neighbor, or purchase [something] from your neighbor, do not cheat one another.
And when you sell sales to your neighbours, or you buy disposable (or moveable) goods from the hand of your neighbours, it is not allowable for a man to defraud his neighbour.
25:15: According to the number of years after the jubilee you shall purchase [land] from your neighbor; according to the number of produce years he shall sell it to you.

Sons of Israel, My people, if you sell a field or a vineyard, according to the sum of the number of years after the Jubela you shall buy of your neighbour; according to the number of years for gathering the produce they shall sell it to you;
25:16: Based on the abundance of years, you shall increase its purchase price and based on the lack of years you shall decrease its purchase price, since it is the number of produce-seasons that he is selling to you.

according to the greatness of the amount of the years shall the price be enlarged; and according to the smallness of the amount of the years the price shall be diminished, because he sells to thee the amount of the fruitage to be ingathered.
25:17: You shall not cheat one another, and you shall fear your God for I am Adonoy, your God.
And you shall not overreach one man his neighbour by hard words, but fear your God: I am the Lord your God.
25:18: You shall fulfill My statutes and keep My laws and fulfill them, and you will then live in the land in security.
And you shall perform My statutes, and observe the order of My judgments and do them, that you may dwell upon the land securely.
25:19: The land will give forth its fruit and you will eat your fill, and you will live securely on it.
And the land will yield her produce, and you shall eat and be satisfied, and dwell upon the land in security.
25:20: If you shall say (ask) What will we eat in the seventh year, for lo! we have not planted nor gathered our produce?
But if you say, What shall we eat in the seventh year; behold, we sow not, nor ingather even the after crop of our provision?
25:21: I shall command (direct) My blessing to you in the sixth year and it will produce [enough] for three years.
I will command My blessing upon you from my treasures of goodness, which are in the heaven of My Presence, in the sixth year, and it will create produce that will suffice for three years.
25:22: You shall plant in the eighth year but you will still be eating from the old produce until the ninth year; until the [new] produce arrives (ripens) you shall eat [from] the old.
But you shall sow in the eighth year, and eat of the old produce of the sixth year until the ninth year; until the time of the incoming of the new produce, shall you eat of the old.
25:23: The land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is Mine, for, you are [merely as] foreigners [foreign resident] and resident aliens [residents] before Me.
And the land of Israel shall not be sold absolutely, for the land is Mine; for you are sojourners and guests with Me.
25:24: In all of your ancestral lands you shall grant redemption to the land.
And in all the land of your possession you shall let the ground have redemption.
25:25: If your brother becomes impoverished and sells some of his ancestral land, and a close relative comes and redeems that which his brother sold.
And if thy brother hath become poor and hath sold his possession, his redeemer who is near of kin to him may come and redeem the sale of his brother.
25:26: [Or] if the man has no redeemer (close relative) but has acquired sufficient means and finds [it] enough to redeem it [himself],
But if a man have no one who is qualified to redeem that which he hath sold, and it befall to his own hand to find the price of its redemption,
25:27: He shall calculate the number of years for which he sold the land and return the remainder (excess) to the man to whom he had sold it, and he shall return to his ancestral land.
then let him count the sum of the years of its sale, and give the amount to the man who bought it, and return to his possession.
25:28: Or if he does not have within his means enough to retrieve the land to himself, then that which he sold remains in the possession of the buyer until the jubilee year. It is then released by the jubilee and he [the seller] returns to his ancestral land.

But if his hand meet not with the price that he should give him, then the property sold shall (remain) in the hand of him who bought it until the year of Jubela, and shall then go out without money, and he shall return to his possession.
25:29: If a man shall sell a residential home [that is] within [surrounded by] a walled city, the time allotted for its redemption shall be until the end of one year after he sold it. He has the days [of a full year] in which to redeem it.
And if a man sell a dwelling-house, in a town surrounded by a wall, it may have redemption until the completing of the year from its sale: from time to time shall be its redemption.
25:30: If he does not redeem it by the end of a full year, the house within the city that is surrounded by a wall shall then remain in perpetuity to its purchaser for his generations (descendants.) It is not released by the jubilee.

But if it be not redeemed at the completing of the full year, the house that is in a walled town shall be confirmed absolutely to him who bought it, unto his generations: it shall not go out at the Jubela.
25:31: The houses of open cities which are not surrounded by a [an encircling] wall shall be considered as a field of the land. It shall have a redemption and it is released by the jubilee.
But houses in villages which have no walls round about them, are to be accounted as tents which are spread upon the fields of the earth; they may be redeemed, and they shall go out at the Jubela.
25:32: The cities of the Levites the houses in the cities of their ancestral land, the Levites shall have an eternal right of redemption.
But the cities of the Levites, the houses of the cities of their possession may be always redeemable by the Levites.
25:33: If anyone redeems [a house or field] from the Levites, then the house or his ancestral city shall be released by the jubilee, for the houses of the Levitic cities are [considered] their ancestral lands among Bnei Yisroel.

And when one hath purchased of the Levites the house that was sold in the cities of their possession, it shall go out at the Jubela; for the houses of the Levites are their inheritance among the children of Israel.
25:34: The field on the outskirts of their cities may not be sold for it is their perpetual ancestral land.
But a field in the suburbs of their cities shall not be sold for it is an everlasting possession for them.
25:35: If your brother becomes impoverished and his hand (assets) become shaky among you, you must support him, [so too] the proselyte [foreign resident] and the sojourner, [so] that he shall live with you.
And if thy brother hath become poor, and his hand wavereth with thee, then thou shalt strengthen and do him good, as a guest and a sojourner he shall be nourished with thee.
25:36: You shall not take from him interest or usury and you shall fear your God, and your brother shall live with you.
My people of the house of Israel you shall not take usuries or remunerations (in his case) but thou shalt fear thy God, and let thy brother have nourishment with thee.
25:37: You must not give (lend) him your money with interest, and usuriously you must not advance him your food.
My people of the house of Israel, you shall not lend him for usury, nor give him your provisions for increase.
25:38: I am Adonoy your God who brought you out from the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan, to be a God for you.
I am the Lord your God, who redeemed and brought you out redeemed from the land of Mizraim, to give unto you the land of Kenaan, and to be unto you Eloha.
25:39: If your brother becomes impoverished and is sold to you, you must not work him like a slave [slaves].
If thy brother with thee shall have become poor, and have sold himself unto thee, thou shalt not make him serve according to the laws of the service of bondmen
25:40: Like a hired hand or resident [worker] shall he be with you He shall serve you until the jubilee year.
but as a hired man and as a sojourner shall he serve with thee, until the year of Jubela shall he serve thee.
25:41: Then he and his children shall depart from you and return to his own family. He shall return to his ancestral estate.
Then shall he go out from thee at liberty, he and his children with him, and return to his family, and to the heritage of his fathers shall he return.
25:42: For they are My servants, whom I brought out from the land of Egypt, they shall not be sold [in the market] as slaves.
For they are My servants whom I brought forth redeemed from the land of Mizraim; they shall not be sold according to the laws of the sale of bondmen.
25:43: You must not rule over him [make him work] to crush him and you shall fear your God.
Neither may you make him serve with rigour, but thou shalt fear the Lord thy God.
25:44: Your slaves and maidservants that you shall possess from the nations that surround you, from them you may purchase slaves and maidservants.
But your bondmen and your handmaids which you may have, of the handmaids of the Gentiles, of them you may purchase bondmen and handmaids.
25:45: Also, from the children of the [uncircumcised] sojourners who reside with you from them you may purchase [slaves], and from their families that live among you that were born in your land. [All these] shall be your permanent possession.

Moreover, of the children of the uncircumcised strangers who sojourn among you, of them you may buy, and of their families that are with you, which they have begotten in your land; but not from the Kenaanaee; and they shall be yours for possession.
25:46: You shall will them as inheritance to your children after you as hereditary property; you shall keep them in servitude permanently. However regarding your bretheren, Bnei Yisroel, man over his brother, you must not rule over him [make him work] to crush him.

And you may leave them to your children after you, to inherit as a perpetual possession; them you shall make to serve: but of your brethren of the sons of Israel no man (may enslave) his fellow; them shall you not make to serve with rigour.
25:47: If a foreigner [an uncircumcised one] or resident acquires means while your brother becomes impoverished by him, and is sold to a [an uncircumcised] resident foreigner who resides with you or to the offspring [a non-Jew] of a foreign [proselyte] family.

And if the hand of the uncircumcised sojourner with you wax strong, and thy brother with him become poor, and sell himself to the uncircumcised stranger who is with thee, or to the stock of a strange religion, to serve him or to worship with him who is of the generation of strangers;
25:48: After he is sold redemption shall be his, one of his bretheren shall redeem him.
when it is known to you that he hath been sold, forthwith redemption shall, be his; one of his brethren shall redeem him;
25:49: Either his uncle [father’s brother] or his uncles son [the son of his father’s brother] (cousin) shall redeem him or the closest (other) family relative shall redeem him. If he obtains sufficient means of his own he may be redeemed [on his own.]

either the brother of his father or the son of his father's brother may redeem him; or a kinsman of the flesh of his family may redeem him; or by his own hand being made strong, or by the hand of the congregation, he may be redeemed.
25:50: He shall reckon with the one who bought him. [According to the number of years] from the year which he was sold to him until the jubilee year. His purchase price shall be [proportional] to the number of years; at the rate of the days of a hired hand it shall be [considered as he worked] with him.

And he shall account with the uncircumcised person who had bought him, from the year that he was sold until the year of Jubela, and the price of his repurchase shall be according to the number of the years; according to the days of an hireling shall it be with him.
25:51: If there are yet many years [until the jubilee] accordingly shall he return his redemption money from his purchase price.
If yet there be many years, according to their number he shall give for his redemption of the money that he was bought for.
25:52: If there remain but a few years until the jubilee year, he shall make a [similar] calculation, based on the number of years he shall return his redemption money [to the purchaser.]
But if few years remain till the year of Jubela, he shall compute with him, and according to the amount of the years give for his redemption.
25:53: As a hired hand [working] on a yearly basis shall he be considered with him; he shall not rule over him [make him work] to crush him before your eyes.
As a hireling by the year shall he be with him, and his master shall not make him to serve with rigour while thou see it.
25:54: If he is not redeemed through these means he then goes out in the jubilee year, he, along with his children.
But if he be not redeemed within those years, he shall go out free at the year of Jubela, he and his children with him.
25:55: For, Bnei Yisroel are My servants. They are My servants whom I have brought out of the land of Egypt, I am Adonoy, your God.
For the sons of Israel are Mine, to obey My laws; servants are they whom I brought out redeemed from the land of Mizraim. I am the Lord your God.
26:1: You shall not make [false] idols for yourselves and graven images and memorial stones you shall not raise up for youselves, and a prostration stone you shall not set in your land upon which to prostrate oneself, for I am Adonoy, your God.

26:2: You shall keep [the days of] My Shabbosos and you shall fear (revere) [the House of] My Sanctuary, I am Adonoy.
The days of My Sabbaths you shall keep, and walk to the house of My sanctuary in My fear; I am the Lord.
26:3: If you follow My statutes and keep My commandments and you will fulfill them,
If you will go forward in the statutes of My law, and keep the orders of My judgments, and perform them,
26:4: I will provide your rains in their proper time. The earth shall give forth its produce and the tree of the field shall give forth its produce.

then will I give you the rains for your lands in your seasons, the early and the late, and the land shall yield the fruits of increase, and the tree on the face of the field shall be prosperous in its fruit.
26:5: [Because of the abundant produce] threshing will overtake the grape harvest and the grape harvest overtake the [time to] plant, and you will eat your bread to satiation and you will live securely in your land.
And with you the threshing shall reach to the vintage, and the vintage unto the springing of the seed, and you shall eat your bread and be satisfied, and dwell securely in your land.
26:6: I will grant peace in the land; you will lie down (sleep) [rest] without disturbance (fear). I will banish [nullify] evil beasts from the land, and no [people who kill with a] sword shall pass through your land.

And I will give peace in the land of Israel, that you may repose, and there be none to disturb; and I will make the power of the wild beast to cease from the land of Israel, and the unsheather of the sword shall not pass through your land.
26:7: You will pursue your enemies and they will fall before you by the sword.
And you shall chase your adversaries, and they will fall before you broken with the sword.

26:10: You will eat the old [store] long kept and the old [store] you will have to clear out because of the new.

but the Glory of My Shekinah shall dwell among you, and My Word shall be to you for a redeeming God, and you shall be unto My Name for a holy people.
26:13: I am Adonoy your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt from where you were slaves, and I broke the bars of your yoke [of the peoples from you] and led you forth standing upright [to freedom].

26:14: And if you will not listen to Me [accept My Word] and you will not fulfill all of these commandments.

26:15: If you despise My statutes and your souls loathe [reject] My laws so as not to fulfill all My commandments, thereby breaking [changing] My convenant.
and if you despise My statutes, and hate in your soul the orders of My judgments, to do not all My precepts, but your purpose be to abolish My covenant;
26:16: Then I will do the same with you. I will impose terror upon you, [which causes] swelling and fever that consume [darken] the eyes and fill the soul with grief. You will plant [your seeds] in vain because your enemies will consume [your crops.]

this also will I do to you: I will draw out against you the smiting pestilence, the flame and the fever, to consume your eyes, and to exhaust life; and ye shall sow your seed in vain, for it shall not spring up, and that which groweth of itself shall your enemies devour.
26:17: I will set my face [anger] against you and you will be defeated [smitten] before your enemies; your foes will rule over you and you will flee [even] when no one is pursuing you.
And I will appoint a reverse to your affairs, and you shall be broken before your foes, and they who hate you shall rule over you; and you will flee when no one pursueth you.
26:18: If after these [catastrophes] you still do not listen to Me [accept My Word], then I will increase your punishment sevenfold, as your sins.
And if after these chastisements ye be not willing to obey the doctrines of My law, I will add to punish you with seven plagues, for the seven transgressions with which ye have sinned before Me.
26:19: I will break the pride [glory] of your power. I will make your [the] heavens [which are above you] like [as strong as] iron [to bring no rain down] and your [the] land [which is beneath you] like [as powerful as] copper [producing no fruit].

And I will break down the glory of the strength of your sanctuary, and will make the heavens above you obdurate as iron, to yield no moisture, nor send you dew or rain, and the ground beneath you to be like brass to put forth (only) to destroy its fruit.
26:20: Your strength will be exhausted in vain. Your land will not yield its produce and the tree[s] of the land will not give forth its produce.
And your strength shall be consumed in vain, for your land shall not yield what you bestow upon it, and the tree upon the face of the field shall drop its fruit.
26:21: If you walk contrary to [before] Me and have no desire to listen to Me [accept My Word], I will increase [to bring] the blows upon you sevenfold, as your sins.

And if you still walk perversely with Me, and will not hearken to the doctrine of My law, I will add to bring upon you (yet) seven plagues, for the seven transgressions with which ye have sinned before Me;
26:22: I will send [incite] among you wild animals of the field and they will make you bereft of children, destroy your cattle, reduce your [population] and make your roads into wasteland.
and I will send against you the strength of the wild beast, to make you childless, and to destroy your cattle without, and to diminish you within, and your highways shall be desolate.
26:23: If after these [catastrophes] you have not been disciplined [to listen] to Me [My Word], and walk contrary to [before] Me,
And if by these chastisements ye will not be corrected before Me, but will walk before Me perversely,
26:24: [Then] I, too, will walk contrary to you; and I shall also smite you seven fold, for your sins.
I will Myself also remember you adversely in the world, and will destroy you, even I, with seven plagues, for seven transgressions with which ye have sinned before Me.
26:25: I will bring [people who kill with a sword] an avenging sword upon you avenging the covenant [and they will avenge from you a vengeance for transgressing the words of the Torah] You will be huddled [in your cities]. I will send [incite] pestilence among you and you will be given into the hand of the enemy.

And I will bring against you a people unsheathing the sword to take vengenance upon you, for that you will have abolished My covenant; and when you are gathered together from the wilderness into your cities, I will send the pestilence among you, or deliver you to die by the hand of your adversaries.
26:26: When I break the staff of your bread [food], ten women will bake your bread in one oven and they will return your bread by weight. You will eat but you will not be satiated.

And when I shall have broken for you the staff of all the subsistence of food, then ten women may bake your bread in one oven on account of its scarcity, and measure and divide it to you diminished in weight, and you will eat and not be satisfied.
26:27: If [in spite] of this you [still] will not listen to Me [accept My Word], and you will walk contrary to [before] Me,
But if by no one correction ye will hearken to the instruction of My law, but will walk perversely before Me,
26:28: I will walk contrary to you in fury, and indeed I too shall punish you sevenfold, for your sins.
I will also remember you adversely in the world, and will chastise you, even I, with seven plagues, for the seven transgressions with which ye have sinned before Me.
26:29: You will eat the flesh of your sons and you will eat the flesh of your daughters.

And ye shall eat the flesh of your sons, and the flesh of your daughters. Mosheh the prophet hath said, How heavy will have been the guilt, and how bitter those sins, that caused our fathers to eat the flesh of their sons, and the flesh of their daughters, because they kept not the commandments of the law!
26:30: I will destroy your high places and I will smash your sun images. I will set your corpses upon the carcasses (remains) of your [false] idols, and My soul [word] will loathe [reject] you.
And I will destroy your high places, and overthrow your diviners and your enchanters, and your carcases will I cast away with the carcases of your idols, and My Word shall abhor you.
26:31: I will turn your cities into ruins and bring your Sanctuaries into desolation. I will no longer scent (accept favorably) the fragrance of your offerings [the offering of your gatherings].
And I will make your cities desert places, and desolate your sanctuary; nor will I receive with acceptance the odour of your oblations.
26:32: I will make the land [so] desolate that your enemies who live on it will be astonished.
And I, even I, will lay your country waste, that the spirit of quietness may not be upon it; so that your enemies who will dwell in it shall be confounded.
26:33: I will scatter you among the nations and unsheath [incite people who kill with] the sword after you. Your land will be desolate and your cities will be in ruins.
And you will I disperse among the nations; for I will stir up against you a people who draw the sword, and your country shall be devastated, and your cities be solitary.
26:34: The land will then be appeased for its Shabbosos [rests] [during] all the days of its desolation while you are in the land of your enemies. Then the land will rest and be appeased for its Shabbosos [rests].
Behold, then shall the land enjoy the years of its Sabbaths all the days that it is forsaken of you, and you are wanderers in the land of your enemies.
26:35: All the days that it lies desolate it shall have its rest—the rest it did not have on your Shabbosos [rests] when you were living upon it.
All the days that it is forsaken by you it shall rest, because it was not at rest in the years of the times for repose when you were dwellers upon it.

And they shall thrust each man his brother, as before them who draw the sword, though none pursue; and you shall have no power of resistance to stand before your adversaries.
26:38: You will be lost among the nations and the land of your enemies will consume you.

26:39: Those of you who survive will rot away [melt] in their iniquity in the land of your enemies, and also due to the iniquities of their [evil] ancestors which are [still] with them [they hold in their hands], [they] will they rot away [melt].

And those who remain of you shall fail (melt away) for their sins in the land of your enemies, and also for the evil sin of your fathers which they held fast in their hands: like them shall they melt away.
26:40: They will [then] confess their iniquities and the iniquities of their ancestors in the unfaithfulness [dishonesty] with which they were unfaithful [dishonest] to [before] Me, and also for walking contrary to [before] Me.

But (when) in the hour of their need they shall confess their sins, and the sins of their fathers, with their falseness with which they have acted falsely against My Word; and that they have acted frowardly also with Me,
26:41: I, too, will go contrary to them and bring them into the land of their enemies. Or perhaps then will be humbled [broken] their uncircumcised (unyielding) [unwise] heart and then their iniquities will be appeased (forgiven).

so that I have remembered them adversely in the world, and brought them into captivity in the land of their enemies; behold, then will their proud heart have been broken, and they will make confession of their sins,
26:42: I will [then] remember My covenant with Yaakov and also My covenant with Yitzchok and also My covenant with Avrohom, I will remember and I will remember the land.

and I will remember in mercy the covenant which I confirmed with Jakob at Bethel, and the covenant which I covenanted with Izhak at Mount Moriah, and the covenant which I covenanted with Abraham, between the divided portions, I will remember, and the land of Israel will I remember in mercy.

But the land shall (first) be relinquished and forsaken you; and enjoy the repose of her remissions all the days that it shall be deserted by you. 26:44: All this not withstanding, even when they are in the land of their enemies I will not despise [abandon] them and I will not loathe [reject] them to annihilate them, to break [change] My covenant with them, for I am Adonoy, their God.
